findings.title: Write lock acquired without re-checking the cache (no double-checked locking)
findings.body: After the fast path under `RLock` sees a nil cache, every goroutine falls through, takes the exclusive `Lock`, and unconditionally re-reads `assets-manifest.json` (or performs the CDN HTTP request) before setting the cache. There is no second check of `entryPointAssetsCache` after the write lock is acquired, so on a cold start with N concurrent requests the manifest is parsed N times, serialized one after another while holding the exclusive lock. Re-checking `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` immediately after `Lock()` makes the load happen exactly once and avoids the serialized duplicate I/O.

findings.title: Cache is overwritten with nil when loading the manifest fails
findings.body: `entryPointAssetsCache = result` runs unconditionally, including when `readWebAssetsFromFile`/`readWebAssetsFromCDN` returned `nil, err`. A transient failure therefore stores nil in the shared cache and the function returns a nil `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` together with the error; any caller that logs the error but still dereferences the returned pointer will panic. Guard the assignment with `if err == nil && result != nil` (and return the previous cached value on error) so a failed reload cannot poison the cache.

findings.title: No test exercising concurrent GetWebAssets calls
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race but adds no test that calls `GetWebAssets` from multiple goroutines, so the race fix is not covered and a future refactor (for example removing the lock or mutating the cached struct) could reintroduce the race without any CI signal. A small `t.Parallel`/`sync.WaitGroup` test run under `-race` would pin the behaviour.
